Rein 0.9.2

Two fixes for the remote Dock, from first field use:

  • Tapping a Dock app now behaves like clicking the real Dock. An app that was running without

any windows (Chrome's background mode) previously activated invisibly — now it opens a fresh

window, and apps that aren't running launch as before.

  • Desktop switching (◀ / ▶ on the phone) actually switches. The keyboard chord is now

synthesized as a real hand would press it — Control key down, arrow, Control up, with the flags

genuine arrow keys carry — which the system's Mission Control layer requires. (Your Mission

Control "Move left/right a space" shortcuts must be enabled in System Settings ▸ Keyboard ▸

Shortcuts — they are by default, even if you normally swipe.)

Rein 0.9.1

Two Rein Remote additions (pair with Rein Remote 0.2.3 on the phone):

  • Switch desktops from the phone. ◀ / ▶ buttons on the trackpad screen move between Spaces —

the same thing as a three-finger swipe on the Mac's trackpad. Uses Mission Control's ⌃← / ⌃→

keyboard shortcut, so it follows whatever you've set there.

  • Dock. A Dock button on the trackpad screen opens a strip of every app that's open on the

Mac, with their real icons and the frontmost app marked. Tap one to bring it to the front —

no more hunting for a window with the trackpad. The control panel's Apps grid shows the real

icons too.

Icons are fetched once per app and cached on the phone, so the live state stream stays as small

as before. Both features work with an older phone or Mac (they simply don't appear).

Rein 0.9.0

Three new features, all asked for by real remote-desk use:

  • Privacy screen. Leave your Mac on for Rein Remote and lock it in person: one click in the

menu-bar panel (or a toggle on the phone) blacks out every screen and ignores the Mac's own

keyboard, trackpad and mouse — while your phone keeps seeing and controlling the real desktop.

Unlock by typing your passcode at the Mac (set it in Rein → Remote) or from the phone. Quitting

or restarting Rein always returns the Mac to normal — the lock can never strand you.

  • Brightness keys drive Rein. The keyboard brightness keys now adjust Rein's unified

brightness (with a matching on-screen indicator), so the keys and Rein's sliders can no longer

disagree about how bright your display is. ⌥⇧ gives fine steps, and the keys act on the display

under your pointer. Turn it off in Displays if you prefer the native behavior.

  • Fan control in the menu-bar panel. Auto/Manual and an RPM slider now live right under the

Fans row in the quick panel, next to the live CPU temperature — no need to open the full window

for a quick manual override.
